newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds aim for 112-07/10 breakout point.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds aim for 112-07/10 breakout point.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures will continue to move higher on Wednesday, and look to test the 112-07/10 area, analysts said.
The market is not expecting any change in U.S. interest rates from the second leg of the FOMC meeting. Any decision was expected around 1815 GMT.
"Yesterday we saw quite a strong recovery after an accelerated downtrend," said Fran Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston.
"I think we'll break back through there to test 112-07/10," Skelley said. "That's the breakpoint for the upside to test (June 20's) 112-24 high, and February's high of 113-09"
By 0925 GMT, the September T-bond was trading 4/32 above Chicago's settlement at 111-26 in automated trade.
"I see support at 111-17," Skelley said. "If there's any deeper dip - and I don't think there will be one - it will be held by the 111-08/04 zone."
She said support at 111-17 stemmed from activity on hourly charts on Tuesday.
Andy Anderson, analyst at Fuji Bank in London, said the market's direction would be dictated by the June payrolls data due to be released on Thursday.
But Tuesday's close above a minor trendline coming in at 111-20 was supportive.
"The market is bullish and as long as it can hold above the low posted on Monday 110-23, then you're going to see higher prices," said Anderson.
He also put the near term target at 112-24.
If 111-23 failed to hold, losses to 111-05 could be foreseen, Anderson said.
December Eurodollars were at 93.955, up 0.005 on the day.
